component.name: Apache Solr
component.description: Lucene-based search server exposing an HTTP/HTTP2 API that indexes documents and serves queries, deployable as a single node or a SolrCloud cluster coordinated by ZooKeeper. It exposes query, update (indexing), and admin/config APIs, supports pluggable authentication and authorization, and can load custom code (package manager, config API, modules). The defining operational fact is Solr's long-standing official stance: Solr is meant to run inside a trusted environment with authentication enabled; an unauthenticated Solr must never be exposed to an untrusted network. The THREAT_MODEL.md is the canonical scanner-facing model; the operator-facing 'Securing Solr' reference guide remains the human source of truth for hardening. SolrJ (the client library) and solr-sandbox (experimental) are out of scope for this model.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.
Operator-facing 'Securing Solr' guide, complementary to the scanner-facing threat model.

blueprints.name: Solr deployment
blueprints.description: The trust boundary is the Solr HTTP API, gated in the supported posture by an authentication plugin and an authorization plugin; once past auth+authz the request is trusted to the extent of the caller's permissions. Query parameters (shards, streaming expressions) can cause Solr to fetch URLs (SSRF surface); admin/config/package APIs can change configuration and load custom code and must be authorization-restricted. In SolrCloud, configuration and cluster state come from ZooKeeper (trusted) and inter-node calls are authenticated (PKI/auth).

assets.name: Solr server / SolrCloud node
assets.description: Search server exposing query (/select) and update (/update) request handlers over HTTP.

assets.name: Admin / Config / Collections / Package APIs
assets.description: Highest-sensitivity surface (/admin/*, ConfigSet/Config API, package manager and blob store): changes configuration and loads custom code; must be restricted to admins via authorization.

assets.name: Authentication and authorization plugins
assets.description: Pluggable authentication (BasicAuth/JWT/Kerberos) and authorization (RuleBasedAuthorizationPlugin); off by default, the security mechanism when enabled.

assets.name: ZooKeeper ensemble (SolrCloud)
assets.description: Trusted config and cluster-state store; securing/ACLing ZooKeeper is the operator's responsibility.

zones.name: HTTP clients
zones.description: Untrusted HTTP clients (in scope only against an intentionally exposed, auth-enabled Solr) and authenticated users bounded by their authorization.

zones.name: Solr trusted environment
zones.description: The trusted environment Solr is meant to run inside: firewalled internal network zone, like a database; never a public-facing zone or DMZ.

zones.name: ZooKeeper ensemble
zones.description: Operator-secured trusted store for configuration and cluster state.

persona.description: In scope only if Solr is intentionally exposed with authentication enabled; an unauthenticated Solr is assumed network-isolated.
Holds credentials; trusted to authenticate but not to exceed their authorization (RuleBasedAuthorizationPlugin permissions).

Trusted: owns all configuration (auth/authz plus any config or configSet manipulation), locks down admin APIs, controls ZooKeeper, the network, and the JVM. There is deliberately no configuration role separate from admin; configuration is an admin-level privilege.

assumptions.description: In the supported posture Solr runs where only authorized clients reach the admin/config/update APIs (authentication enabled and/or network isolation).
Risky features (the historic Velocity response writer, scripting, JEXL, arbitrary remote streaming) are disabled by default and must stay disabled unless the operator accepts the risk.
The ZooKeeper ensemble is a trusted config/state store in SolrCloud; Solr opens network listeners and, via packages/config, can load code by design.

threats.name: Authentication bypass on a protected endpoint
threats.description: API requests require valid credentials when an authentication plugin is configured; an auth bypass on a protected endpoint violates this property. Severity: critical.

threats.name: Authenticated user exceeds authorization
threats.description: RuleBasedAuthorizationPlugin gates paths, collections, and admin actions by permission. An authenticated user performing an action outside their permissions, especially against the admin/config/package APIs, is a critical violation. An over-broad permission authored by the operator is an operator decision, not a Solr flaw.

threats.name: RCE/SSRF reachable in a default configuration
threats.description: Code-execution-adjacent features (Velocity/scripting, arbitrary remote streaming) are disabled by default after Solr's CVE history; RCE or SSRF reachable in a default configuration violates this property (critical). RCE via a risky feature the operator enabled is out of model (non-default config).

threats.name: Rogue actor injects inter-node requests (SolrCloud)
threats.description: Node-to-node calls are authenticated (PKI/auth); a rogue actor injecting inter-node requests violates this property. Severity: high.

threats.name: Unauthenticated Solr exposed to an untrusted network
threats.description: Solr's documented posture is that it runs in a trusted environment behind authentication; an operator who exposes an unauthenticated instance to the internet has violated the deployment contract. Without auth, the admin/config/package APIs let a caller reconfigure Solr and load code, by design, for a trusted operator; this is the number-one real-world Solr incident class and is out of model. Findings whose precondition is reaching an unauthenticated admin/config endpoint over an untrusted network are operator misconfiguration.

threats.name: Configuration change or code loading by an authorized admin
threats.description: The admin/config/package APIs allowing configuration change and custom code loading when reached by an authorized admin (or on an unauthenticated dev instance) is the feature, not a vulnerability; it is only a valid finding when reachable across an auth/authz boundary that should have stopped it.

threats.name: SSRF via shards and streaming-expression remote fetches
threats.description: Query parameters (shards, stream.url, streaming-expression source URLs) can cause Solr to fetch URLs, including internal ones. SSRF is bounded by operator network controls, not by Solr: restricting which hosts Solr may contact is operator/network configuration.

threats.name: ZooKeeper compromise or exposure
threats.description: Solr trusts its ZooKeeper ensemble, which stores configuration and cluster state; an unsecured ZooKeeper is a backdoor into the cluster. Securing and ACLing ZooKeeper is the operator's responsibility, and the ZooKeeper ensemble operator, host, and JVM are out-of-scope adversaries.

trustBoundaries.name: Solr HTTP API trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: A finding is in-model only if reachable with authentication and authorization enabled by an actor who should not be able to do it: an unauthenticated request to an auth-protected endpoint, or an authenticated user crossing their authorization. A finding that requires an unauthenticated, internet-exposed Solr is out of model.

trustBoundaries.name: ZooKeeper trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: ZooKeeper is a trusted config/state store; Solr does not defend against its compromise.

controls.name: Enable authentication and authorization
controls.description: Authentication and authorization are pluggable and off by default; enabling them (BasicAuth/JWT/Kerberos plus RuleBasedAuthorizationPlugin) is what makes the security properties hold. Off-by-default is the insecure default; the supported production posture is auth+authz on, or strict network isolation. Never expose an unauthenticated instance.

controls.name: Never place Solr in a public-facing network zone
controls.description: Keep Solr in a firewalled internal zone, the same way you would a database; Solr is not designed to be internet-facing and must never be placed in a DMZ.

controls.name: Always enable TLS/SSL
controls.description: Enable TLS/SSL for client and inter-node traffic, to avoid leaking sensitive data or authentication credentials on the wire.

controls.name: Lock down the admin/config/Collections/package APIs
controls.description: Restrict the admin, config, Collections, and package APIs to admins via authorization; they change configuration and load custom code.

controls.name: Risky features disabled by default
controls.description: Code-execution-adjacent features (the historic Velocity response writer, scripting, JEXL, arbitrary remote streaming, custom code loading toggles) default to the hardened off/restricted values after Solr's CVE history, controlled among others by -Dsolr.* system properties.

controls.name: Keep risky features disabled
controls.description: Keep risky features disabled unless you accept the risk; an operator who enables them owns the resulting exposure.

controls.name: Restrict remote streaming and shards targets
controls.description: Restrict remote streaming and the shards parameter to known hosts, and apply operator network controls limiting which hosts Solr may contact (SSRF containment).

controls.name: Inter-node authentication (SolrCloud)
controls.description: Node-to-node calls are authenticated (PKI/auth) in SolrCloud.

controls.name: Secure ZooKeeper
controls.description: Secure the ZooKeeper ensemble with ACLs and authentication in SolrCloud; an unsecured ZooKeeper holding Solr config is a backdoor into the cluster.

controls.name: Apply resource/rate limits and keep Solr patched
controls.description: Apply resource and rate limits at the boundary and keep Solr patched.
